entities.summary: The Great Gatsby, a novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald, is a seminal work of American literature that captures the essence of the Jazz Age. Set in the summer of 1922, in the fictional towns of Long Island and New York, the novel explores themes of class, identity, and the corrupting influence of wealth. Through the eyes of Nick Carraway, a young Midwesterner who moves to Long Island to work in the bond business, Fitzgerald masterfully weaves a tale of love, greed, and the American Dream. The novel's vivid portrayal of the excesses and superficiality of the wealthy elite, as well as its critique of the social and economic inequalities of the time, continues to resonate with readers today. The Great Gatsby has been the subject of numerous adaptations, interpretations, and scholarly analyses, cementing its place as a classic of American literature. The novel's influence can be seen in works such as The Catcher in the Rye and The Bonfire of the Vanities, and its themes of class and identity continue to be relevant in contemporary American society.
